clue.text: In France, an offer to study without being asked

parts.note: the French indefinite article 'an' is un
a bid is an offer, as at an auction
a den is a private study or snug room

explanation.surface: A French invitation to study arrives though nobody requested it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unbidden happens without any invitation or request.

clue.text: Biased female abandons terrible ruffian

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of ruffian are wrecked and rearranged
the female letter leaves the jumbled word, walking out on it

explanation.surface: A prejudiced woman walks out on an awful thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes one F out of RUFFIAN, and 'terrible' shuffles the remaining RUFIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased judgment is one lacking fairness or impartiality.

clue.text: Like a bay, perhaps, with a limited view

explanation.surface: A horse in blinkers can see only straight ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: A bay is a reddish-brown horse; racehorses often wear blinkers, eye shields that block side vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse fitted with eye shields is literally so; figuratively, a narrow-minded person sees only part of the picture.

clue.text: Awkward American promises to pay? That's suspicious

parts.note: dub is American slang for a clumsy, inept person, a duffer
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A clumsy American writes out IOUs, which looks shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious and suspicious are synonyms for something doubtful or questionable.

clue.text: Jane accepted one in a lofty retreat

indicators.note: the heroine's name takes in the numeral, as if receiving it inside

parts.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's heroine, so Jane suggests Eyre
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Jane Eyre found a refuge high up.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest is built high on a crag, so it is a lofty hideaway.

clue.text: Student leaves African republic for a place in Europe

indicators.note: leaves means the learner's letter departs from the country's name

parts.note: Liberia is a republic in West Africa
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student quits an African country to settle in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: One robbing a French prime minister around midnight

indicators.note: the statesman's name wraps itself round the middle letter

parts.note: Aristide Briand was several times prime minister of France
the middle of the word night is its letter G

explanation.surface: A thief preys on a French premier late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit who robs travellers.

clue.text: Accountant leaves girl an old musical instrument

indicators.note: leaves means the accountant's letters depart from the girl's name

parts.note: Rebecca is a girl's name
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant walks out, leaving a girl with an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: Attempt first sitar composition, displaying creative ability

indicators.note: first places the rearranged sitar ahead of the attempt
composition means the letters of sitar are put together anew

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Have a go at a sitar piece first, to show off some talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is skill and imagination in making art.

clue.text: Winner leads off Indian Army in a carriage

parts.note: a victor is a winner

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: The champion heads off the Indian Army riding in a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after the queen.

clue.text: One gossips finally of freedom, say, and the gallows

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word of
say signals that the word for freedom is spoken, giving its sound only

parts.note: liberty is freedom
a gibbet is a gallows

explanation.surface: A tattler speaks of liberty and the scaffold.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a flighty, chattering person.

clue.text: Some find the Kirk so mean

definitions.text: Some find the Kirk so mean

indicators.note: some means just a portion of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Churchgoers grumble that the Scottish church is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Kirk (the Church of Scotland) is tiresome to some.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome means tedious or annoying, which is how some find a strict church.

clue.text: Cretans danced in states of ecstasy

indicators.note: danced suggests the letters of Cretans moving about

explanation.surface: Islanders from Crete danced themselves into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Trances are dreamlike, rapt conditions of mind.

clue.text: It's familiar to male cyclists and peevish lawyers

parts.note: cross means irritable, peevish
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: A thing known to men on bikes and to grumpy barristers.
explanation.walkthrough: Men's bicycles have a horizontal top tube between seat and handlebars.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal frame tube on a man's bicycle is called this.

clue.text: She may have a shock — it isn't fair!

definitions.text: She may have a shock — it isn't fair!

parts.words: She may have a shock — it isn't fair!
parts.note: shock means a thick mass of hair, and not fair means dark-haired rather than blonde

explanation.surface: A woman gets a nasty surprise and protests at the injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark hair, rather than fair hair, is so described.

clue.text: Put off, but dined again on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: refed means fed again, dined once more

explanation.surface: Someone postpones, yet eats a second meal on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone.

clue.text: Game played for nothing in the pub

parts.note: free means costing nothing
house, or housey-housey, is an old name for the game bingo

explanation.surface: A round of bingo played without charge in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A FREE HOUSE is a British pub not tied to one brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: A free house is a public house able to sell any brewer's beer.

clue.text: A conspirator in Rome stands up but falls

parts.note: Casca was one of the plotters who stabbed Julius Caesar

indicators.note: in a down answer, stands up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: in the Roman setting, but is the Latin word sed

explanation.surface: A Roman plotter rises to his feet and then topples.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome serves the second piece too: the Latin for 'but' is SED, which 'stands up' turns to DES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascades are waterfalls, water that falls in stages.

clue.text: It sounds when detectives retire

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: retire means draw back, so the detectives' letters run backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Something makes a noise just as the police inspectors go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic was the early sonar used to detect submarines by sending out pulses of sound.

clue.text: Prisoner about to scatter bread in the soup

indicators.note: about means the convict's letters go around the other word

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
to rout an army is to put it to flight, scattering it

explanation.surface: A convict is about to scatter bread into his soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried bread served in soup.

clue.text: Girl played cricket half-heartedly but just as vigorously

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: the doubled central letters are halved, losing one

parts.note: batted means had an innings at cricket

explanation.surface: A girl batted without real effort, yet with undimmed energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle Ts of BATTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated means without lessening in force.

clue.text: Lightweight stories, primarily, in which characters change places?

indicators.note: primarily means the stories come first, ahead of the light weight

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories about someone
a gram is a very light unit of weight

explanation.surface: Trivial tales, mostly, where people swap roles.
explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of wordplay letters are rearranged into new positions.

clue.text: Support the game

definitions.meaning: a span carrying a road over a gap, or the piece holding a violin's strings up
the card game for four players in partnerships

explanation.definitionFit: A bridge holds things up, and contract bridge is a card game.

clue.text: Container holding 60% of the drink in the ship's kitchen

indicators.note: holding means the box encloses the other piece

parts.note: a case is a container

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word keeps its first three letters

parts.note: booze is alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A box with most of the liquor kept in the galley.
explanation.definitionFit: A caboose is a cookhouse on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Possibly a violinist's shady retreat?

definitions.meaning: one who wields a bow, as a fiddler does
a leafy arbour in a garden

explanation.surface: A fiddler's shaded hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a leafy arbour, and anyone who bows a string is literally one.

clue.text: A beautiful girl, but so destructive!

definitions.meaning: British slang for a stunning woman
one who breaks things to pieces

explanation.surface: A gorgeous girl who wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: SMASHER is old British slang for a very attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout beauty is slang for it, and a wrecker who breaks things is literally one.

clue.text: Change course, being unqualified

definitions.meaning: to swerve aside, as a ship does

explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to sheer, and complete or absolute is sheer.

clue.text: Where hill-dwellers may go for a match? Absolutely

definitions.text: Where hill-dwellers may go for a match?
definitions.meaning: people living up a hill descend to the football pitch
completely, perfectly, as in 'suits me' fully

explanation.surface: Upland folk head for the stadium, utterly.
explanation.definitionFit: Descending to a football venue is literal, and the idiom means completely.

clue.text: It's bound to arise

definitions.meaning: to come up or originate, as water from the earth

explanation.surface: Something is sure to come up.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap is a spring, and to originate or rise is to spring.

clue.text: Rip 'em out before the first performance

indicators.note: out means the letters are turned out of order

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Tear them out before opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the opening showing of a play or film.
